title: Recording: Have You Seen My Baby, You’re Sixteen by Ringo Starr | 1973
content:
Sunset Sound Recorders, Los Angeles
Producer: Richard Perry
Engineer: Bill Schnee

Ringo Starr began recording his third studio album, Ringo, on 5 March 1973.

Two tracks were worked on: ‘Have You Seen My Baby’ and ‘You’re Sixteen’.

‘Have You Seen My Baby’ was written by Randy Newman, and originally appeared on his 1970 album 12 Songs. Starr recorded the backing track during this session, with overdubs added on 15 May and 11 July.

‘You’re Sixteen’ was the second single released from the album. The backing track was also completed on this day, with overdubs were added at Sunset Sound the following day. The recording featured Harry Nilsson performing doo-wop backing vocals.

It was completed with a final overdub on 28 March 1973 at Apple Studios in London. Paul McCartney recorded additional vocals, including a kazoo-like solo.

Without any lawyers knowing anything about it, we came back to LA, and in five days had recorded five tracks, which included the three major singles from the album, ‘Photograph’, ‘You’re Sixteen’ and ‘Oh My My’.
Richard Perry
The Record Producers, John Tobler and Stuart Grundy
